title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
authors: Yuntao Bai, Saurav Kadavath, Sandipan Kundu, Amanda Askell, Jackson Kernion, Andy Jones, ... Sam McCandlish, Tom Brown, Jared Kaplan (51 authors, all listed in Further reading)

code.title: ConstitutionalHarmlessnessPaper
code.note: the paper's supplementary repository: the 16 SL and 16 RL principles, the few-shot prompts, the three evaluation sets and sampled responses from five models on 66 prompts; no training code, and no licence file. About 20 minutes for the principles and sample transcripts

takeaway: Trains a harmless, non-evasive assistant with zero human harmlessness labels: critique-and-revise SFT against a written constitution, then RLAIF with AI preference labels distilled into a preference model, Pareto-dominating RLHF.
verdict: Believe the mechanism and the qualitative findings: AI labels can stand in for human harmlessness labels, and the method removes canned refusals (in the released samples, 0 of 2,244 RL-CAI answers against 34% of HH RLHF's). Treat the size of the gain over RLHF as provisional: one run per setup, Elo judged by crowdworkers told to penalise exactly the evasion the RLHF baseline was trained into, no numbers printed in the text, and nothing outside Anthropic can rerun it.

the production constitution used for Claude, showing how the research-era principles evolved (drawing on the UN Declaration of Human Rights, trust and safety practice, DeepMind's Sparrow rules, Apple's terms of service and more).

the 2026 replacement: explanations instead of a list of rules, priorities in order (broadly safe, broadly ethical, compliant with Anthropic's guidelines, genuinely helpful), released under CC0. The reading time is an estimate for the announcement plus a skim of the document.

kb.n: 2022: the RLHF recipe CAI extends; CAI swaps the human preference labels for AI labels (harmlessness only) and keeps the preference model and RL machinery.
2023: removes the preference model and RL entirely; modern pipelines often feed CAI-style AI preference data to DPO-style direct optimisation.
2024: the RL-for-LLMs line that CAI's RLAIF stage belongs to.
2025: replaces preference rewards with verifiable rewards, the other route around human labels.
2020: the few-shot prompting that every stage of CAI relies on to keep the model's output in format.

topics.n: the feedback model as an early LLM judge: calibration, ensembling, chain-of-thought overconfidence.
how Constitutional AI fits into the training of every Claude model, with RLVR and agentic RL on top.
